column1: # Published-artifact drift manifest.
# One row per collaborator-facing document that is authored in this repo and
# published by hand (gsutil) to a public GCS URL. Format: repo_path<TAB>public_url
# Checked by scripts/check-published-drift.sh / .github/workflows/published-drift-check.yml.
# Add a row here whenever a new document gets this treatment -- an entry not
# listed here cannot be checked and will drift silently, same as before this
# existed.
# Known gap, not fixable by adding a row: gs://.../validation/index.html
# ("Validation package", linked from README.md) has no repo source at all --
# authored and uploaded directly, no local copy, no history. Not drift-
# checkable because there's nothing to diff against. Separate follow-up:
# pull a copy into the repo so it has version history and can join this list.
# HARD EXCLUSION -- DO NOT ADD TO THIS MANIFEST OR ANY FUTURE DEPLOY AUTOMATION:
#   gs://regal-scholar-453620-r7-podcast-storage/glmp-v2/viewer_demo/glmp-viewer-demo-v1-v6.html
#   gs://regal-scholar-453620-r7-podcast-storage/glmp-v2/processes/ecoli_lac_operon.json
# Cited by a deposited, DOI-pinned PDF (mermaid-perturbation-design-zenodo.md,
# Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20831780) as of 2026-03-08. The viewer HTML fetches
# the JSON live at request time via ?process=&version= -- there is no "correct"
# repo state to redeploy from, because the repo's own copy of this data has
# already evolved past what the DOI cites. A drift check or a future
# auto-deploy script pushing repo HEAD to either of these two paths would
# silently break a permanent citation. If this content ever needs to change,
# the correct action is a NEW Zenodo record version with the data deposited
# as an attached file, not a GCS overwrite. See snapshot at
# archive/zenodo-doi-20831780-2026-03-08/ for the exact bytes as cited.
